t: Above you, under the glass rotunda at the entrance to the Victoria and Albert Museum, hangs a huge glass sculpture, the V&A Rotunda Chandelier. It's an artwork as much as a source of light. It was made by Dale Chihuly, the American glass artist, well known for taking blown glass into the realm of large-scale sculpture. It was first installed in 1999, then substantially altered and enlarged to its current size in 2001, in time for a V&A exhibition of his work.
